newsitem.title: CANADA: Precision to go back to drawing board on bid.
newsitem.headline: Precision to go back to drawing board on bid.

text.p: Precision Drilling Corp expected to rework its takeover bid for Kenting Energy Services Inc now that Lynx Energy Services Corp could be part of a deal, a Precision official said on Monday.

Precision chief financial officer Dale Tremblay said his firm would need to determine the facts of a proposed merger between Kenting and Lynx, attempt to speak to the firms' boards and likely return with an offer for both oil and gas drilling businesses.
The process was expected to add five days to the 10 days Precision had set before mailing the offer, he said.

Precision, early on Monday, said it would offer C$3.50 cash plus a tenth of one of its shares for each Kenting share, unless Precision stock exceeded C$70 a share on the day before the bid's expiry date. If Precision shares rose above C$70, the value of the exchange would be a maximum of C$7 per share.
However, Kenting, newly spun off from Trimac Ltd, and Lynx also said on Monday that they planned a merger in an apparent defensive move.
Precision chief executive Hank Swartout said later that his firm would welcome the opportunity to acquire both competing drillers at the same time.

"It was a very shrewd move to make the bid before Kenting was trading on a stand-alone basis because no one had a way of valuing it," said Scott Lamacraft, analyst with Sprott Securities. "Now it's actually trading on an ex-distribution basis on the Canadian Dealing Network," he said.

Lamacraft said it was unlikely that Kenting holders would have tendered to the top range of the Precision bid, which was C$10.50 per share with the exchange, when the market was valuing it at about C$12 a share on Monday.
Precision owns 15 percent of Lynx shares, but Tremblay said it was too early to place a value on the company.
The Kenting deal would have been worth about C$400 million.
Precision shares closed up C$4.10 at C$65 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday. Lynx class B stock finished up C$3.60 at C$15.
